result.title: Shaped SAEs: Expanding the Toolkit for Mechanistic Interpretability
result.summary: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) seek to decompose the dense activations of large language models (LLMs) into sparse, potentially interpretable features using a learned overcomplete dictionary. In this work, we ask whether it is possible to enhance the semantic selectivity of the learned dictionary atoms by linearly \emph{shaping} the dense activations prior to learning an SAE. We explore rank-reducing transformations based on the recently introduced J-space corresponding to the averaged Jacobian from the current layer to the LLM output, projecting activations onto the ``live'' subspace spanned by eigenmodes of the Jacobian with larger singular values (which we expect to be more semantically relevant). We also introduce a new approach for training SAEs in which (a)~an affine shaping transformation is learned along with the dictionary atoms, (b)~the atom selection mechanism is based on the TopK projections along the one-dimensional subspace spanned by the atoms, and (c)~reconstruction is carried out using the same atoms. We call this approach a Matched Filter SAE (MF-SAE) based on analogies with communication theory. The promise of shaping is demonstrated via evaluations against dense activations and state-of-the-art SAEs on benchmarks including SAEBench and SAE Probes.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究在训练稀疏自编码器（SAE）前对 LLM 稠密激活做线性「整形」，尝试用基于输出雅可比 J-space 的降秩投影及可学习仿射变换提升字典原子的语义选择性，并在 SAEBench 等基准上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于纯文本可解释性方法，不直接研究 VLM 推理；但其用雅可比「活跃子空间」筛选语义相关方向、并联合学习字典与投影的思路，可能为 LVR 中筛选任务必要视觉信息、约束 latent 状态表示提供可核查线索。
